style.reference_volume: 第二卷：基础、理论和可信性

fonts.math: STIX mathtext (same as volume-two Matplotlib plots)

figures.name: simple-integral
figures.question: How does measuring value groups turn a function into a finite weighted sum?
figures.formula: f(x)=x^2 on [0,1]; s_n(x)=2^(-n)*floor(2^n*f(x)), n=2,4; value-bin preimages have endpoints sqrt(k/2^n). The chapter's height cutoff n is inactive here.
figures.sampling: 801 exact evaluations of f; all exact bin edges and heights for the simple functions. Horizontal segments are separated at jumps; shaded rectangle boundaries are not interpolated function values. The singleton value at x=1 is marked, and endpoint choices do not affect the area.
figures.design: Two aligned panels with identical x/y ranges; warm-yellow shaded rectangles show value times preimage length, dashed neutral curve shows the same target. Widths differ because the bins divide values, not input positions.

figures.name: weighted-projection
figures.question: How can the same candidate space yield different nearest functions?
figures.formula: target x^2 on [-1,1]; best affine projection constants 1/3 under w=1 and 1/2 under w=(1-x^2)^(-1/2)
figures.sampling: 801 uniformly spaced analytic evaluations, including endpoints; the singular weight itself is not plotted.
figures.design: One shared coordinate panel; target neutral, first weight blue dashed, second weight red dash-dot. Same target and candidate space.

figures.name: weak-derivative
figures.question: Does a continuous corner prevent existence of a weak derivative?
figures.formula: f(x)=abs(x), weak derivative g(x)=sign(x) almost everywhere on (-1,1)
figures.sampling: 801 uniform evaluations for f; two exact horizontal segments for g, separated at zero. Open endpoints denote missing classical derivative, not a particular weak representative value.
figures.design: Aligned function and derivative panels, common x scale; no line bridging the discontinuity.

figures.name: covering-centers
figures.question: How do finite representatives cover an uncountable function class?
figures.formula: f_(a,b)(x)=a+b*x, (a,b) in [-1,1]^2; S=(-1,1); d_S equals Euclidean coefficient distance; nine centers at {-2/3,0,2/3}^2, radius sqrt(2)/3
figures.sampling: All nine exact centers. Matplotlib Circle represents geometric closed balls; no claim of a minimal covering.
figures.design: Equal aspect ratio preserves distance balls; candidate boundary neutral, balls warm yellow, grid auxiliary dotted. Center markers disambiguate intersecting circles.

figures.name: budget-active-set
figures.question: How do active constraints differ from positive shadow prices?
figures.formula: min 0.5*||w-(2,1)||^2, w>=0, w1+w2<=tau; exact piecewise coordinate and multiplier formulas from ex:opt-kkt-budget
figures.sampling: 801 uniform points on [0,4], including both switches; tau=0 shown only as the right-limit extension, chapter example assumes tau>0.
figures.design: Two aligned panels share budget x axis and y range; coordinate/multiplier roles explicit in titles; dotted references are switch locations.

figures.name: hull-relaxation
figures.question: Why can a relaxation yield a strictly better objective while the exact hull does not?
figures.formula: integer points S={(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}; left conv(S); right P=[0,1]^2 intersect {x1+x2<=1.5}; maximize x1+x2
figures.sampling: Exact polygon vertices and three integer points. Right highlighted fractional maximizer=(.75,.75).
figures.design: Identical axis limits and equal aspect; optimal faces coral; feasible polygons same shallow fill. Fractional square marker contrasts integer circles.

figures.name: proximal-comparison
figures.question: How do feasibility projection, sparsity thresholding and quadratic shrinkage differ?
figures.sampling: 1201 uniform points on [-3,3], includes -1,0,1; all maps continuous. No smoothing/interpolation of discontinuous maps.
figures.design: Shared input/output panel, solid/dashed/dash-dot lines redundant with colors, direct legend names the operation rather than the color.
